title: Adjectives and adverbs 2 (well, fast, late, hard/hardly)
subtitle: well, fast, late, hard / hardly
summary: Use well as the adverb of good, know that fast, hard and late are both adjectives and adverbs, and understand that hardly means 'very little' or 'almost not'.

lesson.heading: good and well
lesson.text: **Good** is an adjective. The adverb is **well**. We also use well (not good) with past participles: **well-known, well-educated, well-paid, well-behaved**. Well is also an adjective meaning 'in good health'.

examples.text: Your English is **good**. but You speak English **well**.
Sophie is a **good** pianist. but Sophie plays the piano **well**.

lesson.heading: fast, hard and late: adjective and adverb
rows: It's **hard** to find a job right now.
lesson.note: lately = recently: Have you seen Kate lately?

lesson.heading: hardly = very little, almost not
lesson.text: **Hardly** is not the adverb of hard. It means 'very little' or 'almost not'. Compare **hard** (= a lot, with a lot of effort) and **hardly** (= very little). Hardly goes before the verb.

examples.text: Sarah wasn't very friendly at the party. She **hardly spoke** to me.
examples.note: = she spoke to me very little

examples.text: He tried **hard** to find a job, but he had no luck.
I'm not surprised he didn't find a job. He **hardly tried**.

lesson.heading: I can hardly ...
lesson.text: **I can hardly do something** = it's very difficult for me, almost impossible.

examples.text: Your writing is terrible. I **can hardly read** it.
examples.note: = it is almost impossible to read it

examples.text: My leg was hurting. I **could hardly walk**.

lesson.heading: hardly any / anybody / anything / anywhere / ever
lesson.text: You can use **hardly + any/anybody/anyone/anything/anywhere** (= very little, almost none). **Hardly ever** = almost never.

examples.text: *A:* How much money do we have? *B:* **Hardly any**.
These two cameras are very similar. There's **hardly any** difference between them.
The exam results were bad. **Hardly anybody** in our class passed.
She was very quiet. She said **hardly anything**. or She **hardly said** anything.
I'm nearly always at home in the evenings. I **hardly ever** go out.
It's **hardly surprising** that you're tired. You haven't slept for three days.
The situation is serious, but it's **hardly a crisis**.

lesson.text: Hard and hardly are not a pair like quick and quickly. 'He works hard' = a lot of effort; 'He hardly works' = almost never.

exercises.prompt: Joe's exam results were very ___. Joe did ___ in his exams.
exercises.explanation: Good is the adjective (results were good); well is the adverb (he did well).
Well is the adverb: it says how I slept.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the well- word that completes it.

pairs.left: I'm surprised you haven't heard of her. She is quite ...
Our neighbours' garden is neat and tidy. It is very ...
I enjoyed the book. It's a great story and it's very ...
Tanya knows about everything. She is very ...
Jane works very hard in her job, but she isn't very ...
The children were very good. They were ...

exercises.prompt: Slow down! You're walking too ___ for me.
exercises.explanation: Fast is both an adjective and an adverb; there is no word 'fastly'.

exercises.statement: I haven't been to the cinema late.
exercises.explanation: I haven't been to the cinema lately. Lately means 'recently'; late means 'not on time'.

exercises.prompt: I tried ___ to remember her name, but I couldn't.
exercises.explanation: I tried hard = I tried a lot, with a lot of effort. Hardly would mean 'almost not'.

exercises.prompt: Scott and Tracy have only met once before. Put the words in order.
exercises.explanation: Hardly goes before the verb: they hardly know each other.

exercises.prompt: You're speaking very quietly. I can ___ you.
exercises.explanation: I can hardly hear you = it is almost impossible for me to hear you.

exercises.prompt: I don't feel good this morning. I ___ last night.
exercises.explanation: Hardly goes before the verb: I hardly slept = I slept very little.

exercises.statement: This coat is practically unused. I've hard worn it.
exercises.explanation: I've hardly worn it. Hardly = very little, almost not.

exercises.prompt: It was a very warm day and there was ___ wind.
exercises.explanation: Hardly any wind = very little wind, almost none.

exercises.prompt: I listen to the radio a lot, but I ___ watch TV.
The hotel was almost empty. There was ___ staying there.
exercises.explanation: Hardly anybody / hardly anyone = very few people.
